# WORLD — *The Long Book*

The Shelf, in the year 1219 of the Reckoning.

---

## Cosmology & History

There is no pantheon on the Shelf worth the name. There is the tide, which
is reliable, and the Whiting, which is not, and between them a city that has
spent two hundred years persuading itself that dirt forgives.

The founding fact is geological, not divine. The river Nissa comes down out
of Kethren carrying more salt than a river should, because the uplands are a
sour country, and where it meets the sea it has built forty miles of flats
that nothing grows on: **the Whiting**. The Shelf's whole civilisation is
the answer to one question — *where do you put what you take out?* — and for
twelve centuries the answer has been *there*.

**Timeline**

| Year | Event | Why it still hurts |
|---|---|---|
| c. 700 | First recorded pairs. Drawers and setters work as a village trade, unlicensed, paid in kind. | The fen still remembers this as the honest era and says so at every funeral. |
| c. 1010 | The Whiting **warranted** as common sink by the river towns. First cairns walked. Set-downs elsewhere forbidden. | The warrant is the instrument the Reckoning House still administers. Every carry in the Long Book is ultimately secured against the Whiting's capacity. |
| 1004–1041 | The **Reckoning House** founded at Amrith, on the Stone Ait, to measure capacity, standardise the **carry**, and hold the Long Book. | Turns a trade into a currency. From here, a person with capacity is a person with a credit rating. |
| 1063 | The **Third Order** enacted: the law of composition. An unpayable assessment may be settled by merging the debtor's estate into the creditor's through a witnessed marriage. | This is the instrument that holds Sahra Ottun. |
| 1104 | The **Kethren Concession**: upland farms may not hire Shelf pairs, to keep capacity in the delta. Kethren has done everything by hand and lime ever since. | Why Yannu's people are poor, why setters born upland come down, and why the uplands feel about the House the way an occupied country feels about a garrison. |
| 1148 | The **Sur Ellun trials.** The House attempts to warrant a second sink on the outer isles. Set-downs into moving water fail; eleven setters die; the isles are abandoned. | The reason nobody has looked for a second sink since. It is settled science that there is no alternative to the Whiting. |
| **1200** | **The Nesuir Failure.** Ines Ottun, contracted to draw blight out of the Nesuir seed-granaries at Ferrey, founders at the eleventh carry. The blight seats in her and returns to the grain. Four thousand quarters of seed lost. | The barrier's date. |
| **1201** | **The Hungry Year.** No planting on the middle Nissa. The Sarrow fen eats its stock. Assessment entered against Ines Ottun and *the drawing line of Ottun*: **2,140 carries**. | The debt. Sahra was nine. She was fed by people who had nothing, and she has never once been allowed to forget it, mostly by herself. |
| 1203 | Ines Ottun dies, three years foundered, carrying blight. | Sahra watched it. It is why she knows what the end looks like. |
| 1210 | Veth Dral, bond-setter under indenture to a salt-factor, is worked to full grey at 28 and walks out onto the Whiting. | Yannu's ghost. |

Security pledged: the Sarrow common ground and the drawing line of Ottun. | Sahra was nineteen. She signed it herself. Nobody made her. |
| 1213 | Yannu Dral takes the walker's warrant for the eastern lobes. | |

| **1219** | The book. | |

## Magic System — Hard Rules

The trade is called **the Draw**. It has two halves and no third.

**HR-1 — A load is a quality, not a substance.** A working takes a
*condition* out of a thing: the salt from a cistern, the rot from a granary
bay, the fever from a ward, the blight from seed, the souring from a hold.
The thing is left clean. Nothing is added anywhere. The condition simply
changes what it is in.

**HR-2 — Only a drawer can draw; only a setter can set.** Both are born to
it. Draw runs at roughly one in four hundred births on the Shelf; set at one
in three thousand. Neither can be taught, bargained for, or acquired. The
scarcity of setters is the single most important economic fact in this world.

**HR-3 — A load can only be carried by a body.** Between the thing it came
out of and the ground it goes into, a load lives in a drawer, and it is felt
there. It sits where the body will hold it: salt in the blood, rot in the
joints, fever in the marrow, blight in the nails and hair, souring in the
lungs. The sensations are fixed and specific (see §Costs).

**HR-4 — Capacity is finite, personal, and measured in carries.** A
**carry** is the House's standard unit: the salt of one cistern of two
hundred barrels, or the rot of one granary bay, or the fever off nine
people. An ordinary drawer holds three or four. A strong one holds eight or
nine. Sahra Ottun holds fourteen, which is one short of the record in the
Long Book, and the man who set the record foundered proving it.

Past capacity, a drawer **founders**: the load stops being carried and
becomes the drawer's own condition, permanently. A foundered drawer keeps
what they were holding for the rest of their life and their capacity does
not recover. There is one sign and it is the only sign: **the thirst stops.**

**HR-5 — A setter passes; a setter cannot hold.** A set requires three
things: ground that will take it, skin against skin, and time. The setter
puts his hands on the drawer, opens the ground, and the load goes through
him. He cannot stop it partway, cannot store it, cannot take it off a drawer
and walk away with it.

**HR-6 — What passes through a setter leaves grey.** Permanent loss of
sensation, beginning at the fingertips and moving inward, at roughly one
fingerbreadth — a **span** — per two hundred carries passed. Grey is
reported as a location: *to the second knuckle. To the wrist. To the elbow.*
It never comes back.

**HR-7 — A load taken fast jumps.** More than three carries in a single pass
and the loss does not stay in the hands. It goes to the nerve and lands
where it lands: a taste, a smell, the sight in one eye, the feeling in a
foot. Bond-setters — indentured setters worked at speed for factors — are
made this way, and die of it, because a man who cannot feel a wound does not
treat one.

**HR-8 — A load moves one way only: thing → drawer → setter → ground.** It
cannot pass from drawer to drawer, from setter to setter, or from setter
back to drawer. There are no relays. There is no lending. This forecloses
every clever arrangement anyone has thought of in twelve hundred years.

**HR-9 — Only dead ground takes.** The Whiting takes. Living ground takes a
load only by dying, and it dies widely and slowly and the load surfaces
again within a generation. Setting into living ground is the gravest crime
in the Third Order and is treated as arson.

**HR-10 — Setting requires still ground and low water.** No set is possible
into moving water — the Sur Ellun trials settled that at the cost of eleven
setters — and no set is possible above the tideline of the working flats.
The whole rhythm of the Shelf runs on this: workings happen at low water,
and the year's biggest workings happen at the year's lowest tides, in
Deepwinter.

**HR-11 — A carried load can be read.** Any drawer can see what another is
carrying, from the whitening in the cuticles or the sweetness at the wrist
or the wet look of the eye. The House employs **assessors** whose entire
work is looking at people. There is no other form of remote observation in
this world — no scrying, no familiars, no sending. The surveillance here is
a clerk with good eyes and a ledger.

**HR-12 — What the world believes about ground, and where it is wrong.**
The Shelf holds that a set-down *ends* a load: the ground has it, and the
ground is infinite because the ground is the ground. This is HR-9 misread
for two centuries. Ground does not end a load. **Ground carries it, exactly
as a body does — and ground has a capacity.** The Whiting has been drawing
on its own capacity since 1010 and is now foundering, in the technical sense
of HR-4: what it was carrying is becoming what it is. That is what the
returns in the fen are. Nothing has been destroyed since the trade began.
Everything has been stored.

**HR-13 — The one place a load genuinely ends.** A setter does not merely
conduct. He keeps a fraction of every load, permanently, and what he keeps
stops being a load and becomes his numbness. **Grey is not damage. Grey is
the load, finished.** The Shelf has had the answer in its hands for twelve
hundred years and has classified it as an occupational injury. This is
established physically from ch 2 (Turi Osse: *"It isn't gone, boy. It's in
me."*) and named as a mechanism in ch 36.

---

## Magic System — Costs, Limits, and Prices

### What it costs to work

**To draw:** you carry it, and you feel it, in the fixed signatures below,
until a setter takes it off you. Days, usually. Weeks, if you are unlucky or
unwarranted.

- **Salt** — sits in the blood. Thirst that water does not touch. Whitening
  at the hairline and in the cuticles. A coin taste at the back of the
  throat. Skin that squeaks faintly under a thumb.
- **Rot** — sits in the joints. A sweetness at the wrists you can smell
  across a table. A give in the knees like wet rope. A slow turning-over
  sound in the ear.
- **Fever** — sits in the marrow. Wet-looking eyes. Cold hands, hot
  breastbone. A hum in the back teeth.
- **Blight** — sits in the nails and hair. Ridged nails lifting at the bed.
  Hair coming out at the temple. A smell of cut grass gone over.
- **Souring** — sits in the lungs. A cough with no sickness under it. A
  taste of standing water.

**To set:** cold from the inside of the hand outward, then hot, then
nothing, with a whine pitched at the jaw. Afterwards, a span of grey per two
hundred carries, permanent, and a jump if taken fast (HR-7).

### What it cannot do

- It cannot destroy. Only move, and — unrecognised — finish, in a setter
  (HR-13).
- It cannot heal a wound, mend a bone, or restore a lost sense. It takes
  *conditions*: fever, rot, souring. It does not take a cut or a break or a
  grey hand. Nothing in this book undoes anything.
- It cannot be done alone. A drawer without a setter is a person with a
  disease they chose.
- It cannot cross moving water, work above the tideline, or run in relay.
- It cannot be taught, inherited by intent, transferred, or bought. It can
  only be *hired* — which is why the Shelf's entire law of obligation is
  built around hiring bodies for terms.

### The price list

These are the numbers the book will be paid in. They are set here before the
outline knows what it wants from them.

| Transaction | Price, in the system's own currency |
|---|---|
| One carry taken and set | Drawer: days of the load's signature. Setter: 1/200 span of grey. |
| A working past capacity | Foundering: permanent retention of the load, permanent loss of capacity. Irreversible. |
| A fast set (>3 carries in one pass) | A jump: one sense or one region, permanently. Irreversible. |
| **Binding yourself to another person** | On the Shelf, marriage is a merger of accounts. What it costs is your capacity: your future carries become the joint estate's asset, pledgeable by your spouse's house against its own obligations. You are, from the witnessing, collateral. |
| **Breaking such a binding** | The composition voids. The original assessment revives at full value with accrued charge, and the pledged security is distrained — which means the people and land pledged behind you, not you. |
| **Giving power away** | Impossible directly (HR-8). The only instrument is a **bond-setter's indenture**: twenty years of your hands, sold, at whatever speed the buyer wants them worked. Current market: about 280 carries' credit for a setter of Yannu's grey. |
| **Extending a life** | Not possible. Fever can be drawn out of a body; age cannot. |
| **Ending a load permanently** | A setter's grey, at the rate of what he keeps. Full grey — touch, taste, smell, gone to the root — is what about two thousand carries in one continuous pass costs a man. |
| **Crossing the line between these two** | 2,140 carries, or a house of standing willing to assume them. |

## Magic System — Societal Implications

**1. Capacity is credit, and the body is the collateral.** The Reckoning
House does not lend coin; it records obligations denominated in carries and
enforces them. Every person of capacity has an entry. A drawer's assessed
capacity is their credit rating, published quarterly, and it is why Sahra
conceals her single early foundering: an assessor who knew would strike her
rating, and a struck rating is a smaller instalment and a longer sentence.

**2. Water, grain, and medicine are all one industry, and it is a debt
industry.** Amrith drinks because drawers desalt its cisterns; it eats
because drawers keep the granaries; it survives its fevers because drawers
work the wards. All of that is financed on carries. A collapse in the value
of a carry is a collapse of the water supply, the food supply, and the
hospitals in a single season. This is the whole of Bel Osse's argument, and
she is right about it.

**3. Setters are the scarcest thing in the world and are treated
accordingly.** A setter can name their price and, in the same breath, be
bought outright. The **bond-setter's indenture** — twenty years of hands,
worked at the buyer's chosen speed — is legal, common, and the largest
single source of factor wealth. Kethren exports setters the way it once
exported wool. Full-grey setters are pensioned by ordinance and die early of
injuries they never felt.

**4. Class runs on grey and thirst.** You can read a person's trade off
their body at ten paces: the whitened hairline of a cistern drawer, the
sweet wrists of a granary hand, the gloved hands of a setter hiding how far
he has gone. The rich are the people who have never carried anything.

**5. Disability is reorganised.** A person the Draw cannot help — a broken
back, a lost eye, a deaf child — is outside the whole economy, because the
trade takes conditions and not damage. There is a large, articulate, poor
class of people the Draw has nothing to offer, and they do the old work by
hand: washers, limers, spoilers' men. Sefa Quenn is one of them.

**6. Courtship, marriage, inheritance, kinship — the machinery this book
collides with.** See the next section; this is the implication that matters
most and it gets its own.

---

## Geography

**Amrith** — the delta city at the Nissa's mouth. Eighty thousand people on
timber and shell. Three parts:

- **The Stone Ait**, an island of grey limestone in the second reach, the
  only stone in the delta, where the Reckoning House stands. Sensory: dry
  air, lamp oil, the sound of a hundred pens, and the particular silence of
  people who are being assessed.
- **The Low Wharfs**, the working city, which floods at every second tide
  and has been built to expect it — stairs that go down into water, doors on
  the upper floor. Sensory: wet rope, fish-lime, tide-bells at every corner,
  the smell of a street that dries out twice a day.
- **Kell Ammar**, the salt-house district at the eastern edge, where the fen
  crews sleep between workings. Sensory: coarse salt underfoot like sugar on
  a table, one lamp per room, eleven people breathing.

**The Whiting** — forty miles of dead flats east of the city. White, level,
and loud: the crust ticks as it cools, like a hearth. No birds. Air that
dries the eye in a minute. Landmarks: the **Nine Marks** (walkers' cairns),
the **Shell Bank** (a two-mile ridge of dead cockle where Yannu keeps a hut),
and the **Wallow** (the northern lobe, where standing water has appeared in
the last six years, and where nothing standing has any business being).

**The Sarrow** — six fen villages between the Third and Fifth Reaches:
Sarrow-under-Wall, Little Sarrow, Ferrey, Wick, Ounds, and the station at
Kell Ammar. About 1,900 people. Tenure runs through House Nesuir. Sensory:
black water, sedge, methane off the mud at low tide, the church-quiet of a
place with no stone in it.

**Kethren** — the uplands, nine days up the Nissa by barge and four back
down. Sour terraced soil worked by hand and lime under the 1104 Concession.
Setters are its chief export and the fact is a wound there. Sensory: cold
stone, woodsmoke, lime dust in the throat, and the deliberate absence of
anything a drawer would be paid for.

**Sur Ellun** — the outer isles at the Shelf's lip, two days' sail, where
the sea goes suddenly deep. Abandoned since 1148. Sensory: wind with no
shelter, birds again, water that never stops moving.

**Distances that matter:** Amrith to the Whiting's edge, half a day by punt
and three hours on foot. Amrith to the Sarrow, two days upriver. Amrith to
Kethren, nine days up. Amrith to Sur Ellun, two days' sail. These are what
make separation expensive: a letter to Kethren and an answer is a
three-week silence, and Yannu's mother's letters are always three weeks old
when they arrive.

**The calendar:** ten months of thirty-six days — Thaw, Green, Highwater,
Longsun, Dust, Ebb, Whitening, Rime, Deepwinter, Turn. The year's lowest
tides fall in Deepwinter, which is when the largest workings are done.

---

## Factions & Politics

**The Reckoning House.** Not a government; something worse. It holds the
Long Book, assesses capacity, standardises the carry, warrants ground, and
enforces obligations denominated in carries. It can compel any name in the
Book onto a **standing order** — impressment at one third the open rate —
whenever it declares a hazard. It cannot tax, raise troops, or make law; it
does not need to. Chief Reckoner: **Bel Osse**. What it can do to Sahra:
compel her labour, publish her rating, distrain her security. What it can do
to Yannu: strike him from the walkers' roll, which means assessment, which
means retirement, which means he loses the only work he thinks is worth
doing.

**The great houses — Nesuir, Ammar, Dell.** Landed creditors. They hold fen
tenancies and granaries and they finance plantings against future carries.
House Nesuir is the smallest of the three and the most exposed, because it
took the Ottun assessment onto its own books in 1211 and has been carrying
it since. Matriarch: **Dovra Nesuir**. What it can do to Sahra: everything,
and it will do it slowly and in writing.

**The salt-factors.** New money out of the cistern trade. They buy
bond-setters and work them fast. They are the reason full grey exists as a
common condition rather than a rare one. No single leader; a guild-hall and
a habit. They are the faction Yannu has spent six years refusing, at cost.

**The fen.** The Sarrow's six villages, administered by a fen-reeve elected
for three years. Reeve: **Ansa Rask**. They have no instrument of power at
all except the fact that their tenure is what secures other people's
obligations, which means they are always the collateral and never the party.
What the fen can do to Sahra: nothing, formally. Which is precisely why she
cannot leave it.

**Kethren.** A subject upland with a grievance, a hundred years of exported
setters, and no leverage since the Concession. Its people in Amrith are a
visible underclass who do the sets nobody else will.

**The handworkers.** Washers, limers, spoilers' men — the trades the Draw
made unaffordable rather than obsolete. Not organised. **Sefa Quenn** is
their memory, which is not the same as their leader.

---

## Courtship, Kinship & Consent

**What marriage is for here.** A witnessed marriage on the Shelf is a
**merger of accounts**. Two estates become one; assets, tenancies,
obligations and *future capacity* pool. Love is not irrelevant — the Shelf
is sentimental about it in songs — but nobody confuses it with the
instrument. A marriage is drawn up by clerks, witnessed by the House, and
entered in the Long Book, and the entry is the marriage. The ceremony is a
reading of the entry aloud.

**Who arranges it.** For those with entries in the Book, the houses do, or
the House does. For everyone else, people arrange it themselves and the
Book records it afterward for the sake of the tenancy.

**What it transfers.** Everything, including what has not happened yet. A
drawer who marries pledges her future carries into the joint estate, where
her spouse's house may pledge them forward as security against its own
obligations. This is the pivot on which the whole book turns.

**Who is dishonoured by breaking it.** Not the couple — the *security*.
Because compositions pledge third parties, breaking one is not a scandal, it
is a foreclosure. The village whose common ground stood behind you loses its
tenure. The child whose capacity was named in the schedule is set to the
pump. The Shelf regards a broken composition the way another world regards a
bank run: not as immorality, as damage.

**Composition, under the Third Order (1063).** Where an assessment cannot be
paid within the debtor's working life, a creditor may take it onto their own
books in exchange for a witnessed merger. The debtor's carries are credited
internally at the house's rate. The debtor's dependents are held harmless
while the composition stands. Compositions may be **deferred** — the
instrument executes on witnessing, and witnessing may be set years out — and
they may be **accelerated**: on a material change in the value of the pledged
security, the creditor may demand execution within thirty days. That clause
is printed on the face of every composition on the Shelf and nobody reads it
until it is used.

**Bonds, mates, and ties: there are none.** This world has no soul-bond, no
mate-mark, no tie between people that the Draw makes. What one person can
know of another is what HR-11 permits: a drawer can *read a load* off a body
— what you have been carrying, roughly how much, for roughly how long. That
is all. **It reports a fact, never a feeling.** Nothing in this world can
tell anyone that anyone is theirs, and no character may be given that
knowledge by any means.

**Consent, and the world's own answer.** A composition is signed by the
debtor, in person, before a reckoner, and cannot be signed for her. Sahra
signed hers at nineteen and nobody made her — that is the source of its hold
on her and it is deliberate. The Third Order gives her one refusal, at the
witnessing, spoken aloud: **any party may refuse at the reading.** The
refusal is recorded, the composition voids, and the security is distrained
the same day. So the world's answer to *who may refuse* is: anyone, always,
out loud, at a price paid entirely by other people. That is the shape of
coercion here. Nothing compels her body and nothing touches her will. The
instrument simply arranges the world so that the free choice costs 1,900
people their tenure and a fourteen-year-old girl twenty years at the pump.

Consent between the two leads is never at issue and is never treated as an
obstacle: Sahra says what she wants when she wants it, out loud, and so does
Yannu, and the tragedy is that saying it changes nothing about the schedule.

---

## Proximity & Adhesion

They meet because the Reckoning House puts them in harness, and they stay in
harness because only the House can take them out.

In Green 1219 the Wallow weeps into the Third Reach on a flood tide. The
House declares a hazard and issues a **standing order** under its warrant
power: one drawer of capacity and one warranted walker, paired, on the
House's account, to survey the lobe and stop the weep. It names Sahra Ottun,
because her name is in the Long Book and the House may compel any name in
it. It names Yannu Dral, because he is the only walker who has mapped the
north lobe and because Bel Osse wants him where she can see him.

**Why neither can simply stop showing up.** Sahra's carries are pledged;
absence from a standing order is a default on the composition, which
distrains the Sarrow. Yannu's warrant is the House's to strike, and a struck
walker is assessed, and an assessed walker with grey past the wrist is
retired. Neither of them has a version of walking away that costs only
themselves.

**What contact costs each of them.** Sahra works at the impressment rate,
one third of open hire — so every day beside him is a day her debt clears
more slowly, and she does that arithmetic in ch 5 and hates him for it. She
also cannot conceal her carrying from him (HR-11), and he counts more
honestly than the assessors do. Yannu spends grey on the House's business
that he has spent six years refusing to spend on anything but need, and
signs warrants he does not believe, and every span he gives to this survey
is a span he cannot give to the sets he thinks are worth doing.

**What would have to break for them to lose contact.** The standing order
discharged — which requires the weep stopped, or the House releasing it, or
one of them foundering or going grey past working. Nothing else. Not
distance, not anger, not the witnessing. They are, for ten months, each
other's job.

---

## The Barrier's Machinery

### The instrument

**The Ottun Composition**, contracted 1211 under the Third Order, between
House Nesuir (creditor) and Sahra Ottun (debtor), against the assessment of
1201: **2,140 carries**, entered in the Long Book against Ines Ottun and the
drawing line of Ottun.

- **Terms.** Nesuir carries the assessment on its own books. Sahra works
  carries, credited internally at Nesuir's rate. On witnessing, Sahra Ottun
  and Halim Nesuir marry, the estates merge, the Ottun entry ceases to exist
  as a separate obligation and becomes an internal charge.
- **Security pledged.** (a) The Sarrow common ground — six villages, about
  1,900 people, whose tenure runs through the Nesuir estate. (b) The drawing
  line of Ottun: presently Sahra, and after her Yeshin Ottun, aged fourteen,
  to be assessed at sixteen.
- **Balance at ch 3.** 1,806 carries outstanding after eight years. At her
  achieved rate — 334 carries in eight years, and lower now she has been
  impressed at a third — she clears it at sixty-two.
- **Acceleration.** On a material change in the value of the pledged
  security, the creditor may demand execution within thirty days. Printed on
  the face. Invoked in ch 32.

### Who enforces it, and who benefits

The **Reckoning House** administers the Book and would distrain; **Dovra
Nesuir** is the party with standing to demand. Dovra benefits, and so does
every tenant of Nesuir, and so — for as long as it holds — does the Sarrow.
Nobody in this arrangement is being greedy. Dovra took a ruinous assessment
onto a small house's books in 1211 and has been carrying it for eight years,
and she has since pledged the composition *forward* as security against
Nesuir's own obligations to the House. If Sahra walks, Nesuir is exposed,
Nesuir calls in its fen tenancies to cover, and the Sarrow goes anyway. The
creditor cannot release the debtor without destroying the same people the
composition protects. That is not a villain's trap. That is what a small
house's balance sheet looks like.

### What breaking it costs each of them

**Sahra:** the composition voids; the 1201 entry revives at 2,140 with eight
years' accrued charge; the Sarrow's tenure is distrained; Yeshin is assessed
at sixteen against a live entry and set to the pump — twenty years bonded
drawing in the cistern works, which founders drawers by thirty. And Sahra
herself becomes what her grandmother was: the Ottun who cost the fen
everything.

**Yannu:** he has nothing pledged and nothing to lose in the instrument,
which is the humiliation. He is not a party. He cannot be made a party. The
only door the Third Order leaves him is **assumption** — a house of standing
may assume an assessment — and he is not a house; he is a man with a hut on
a shell bank and a warrant the House can strike. The one instrument
available to a man with no estate is the bond-setter's indenture: twenty
years of his hands, sold at the buyer's speed, raising about **280 carries**
against **2,140**. He works this out at a factor's desk in ch 28 and the
arithmetic is the answer.

### The conversation that would dissolve it

There is one, and it has three possible parties, and the book has all three
of them on the page before the halfway mark, because a barrier that survives
only while nobody asks is not a barrier.

1. **Sahra to Dovra Nesuir (ch 10, 22%).** *Release me.* Dovra says yes:
   bring me 2,140 carries or a house that will assume them. Then she opens
   the Nesuir book and shows her why. Sahra can read a ledger. She leaves
   understanding the arithmetic better than she did going in, which is worse.
2. **Sahra to Halim Nesuir (ch 17, 37%).** *Release me.* Halim would, in an
   instant, and says so, and means it. He cannot: release is not his to
   give. The composition is between estates and the estate is his mother's
   while she lives, and the forward pledge to the House stands regardless of
   who holds Nesuir. He offers her the only thing in his gift — that he will
   never touch her, and she may live as she likes — and it is a kindness,
   and it is the worst thing anyone says to her in the book.
3. **Yannu to anyone (ch 28, ch 33).** *Let me take it.* He is not a party,
   he cannot be made one, and the instrument that would let him try raises an
   eighth of the sum and costs him twenty years of hands.

**Why neither lead can end it by talking.** Not because they are proud, or
withholding, or waiting for the right moment. They ask. They ask early and
they ask plainly and they are answered honestly by people who are not
lying to them. The barrier is not a misunderstanding; it is a sum. The only
sentence that would end it is *here are 2,140 carries*, and no living
person can say that sentence, because 2,140 carries is more than any drawer
in the history of the Long Book has taken in a working life.

### Its dependence on the Draw

If the Draw vanished tomorrow, this barrier would not weaken; it would
**cease to exist**, and it would do so instantly and completely, because
every load-bearing part of it is made of the Draw and nothing else.

Begin with the instrument. The Ottun entry is not an amount of value; it is
an amount of **capacity** — 2,140 carries, a quantity of a bodily faculty
that only certain people possess and that no market can substitute for.
Delete the faculty and the number on the page is not a smaller debt or an
awkward debt; it is a measurement in a unit that no longer measures
anything, like a lien denominated in a colour. There is no exchange rate to
fall back on, because the Shelf never built one: the carry *is* the Shelf's
unit of account, and it is the unit precisely because it cannot be
manufactured, stored, transported, or held by anyone but the person who was
born able to hold it. Next, the office. The Reckoning House is not a
treasury with a sideline in magic; it is an assay office for a faculty. Its
assessors do one thing — look at bodies and say what they are carrying — and
its Book records one thing, and its warrant power exists to allocate one
scarce good. Remove the faculty and the House does not become a court; it
becomes a building full of clerks with nothing to count, and the Third Order
becomes a procedure for merging estates that have no reason to merge. And
finally, the reason it runs to a *marriage* at all. Compositions exist
because capacity is the one asset on the Shelf that cannot be conveyed. You
cannot sell a carry, ship it, warehouse it, or leave it in a will. It exists
only in a body, and it descends only through a body: capacity runs in
bloodlines, which is why the 1201 assessment attaches to *the drawing line of
Ottun* and not to a parcel or a purse. An asset that can only be transferred
by producing a person who has it can only be pledged through the instrument
that produces people — which is marriage, and which is why the Shelf's
entire law of debt is written in the language of betrothal rather than of
sale. Take away the Draw and you take away heritable capacity; take away
heritable capacity and the debt has no reason to follow Yeshin, no reason to
be settled in a marriage rather than a payment, and nothing left to attach
to at all. The writ would be waste paper, the enforcing office would have no
function, and the whole chain of obligation from Ines Ottun's eleventh carry
to Sahra's witnessing would be void. There is no version of this book in
which these two people are kept apart by a bad contract that happens to sit
near a magic system. The contract is *made of* the magic system. That is the
design, and it is why the book is worth writing.

---

## Private Space

There is no scrying on the Shelf and no magical eye. What there is instead
is **HR-11** — every drawer can read what every other drawer is carrying —
and a bureaucracy that writes things down. A composed drawer must record
every carry. A warranted walker must file every warrant. Assessors sit at
the wharf ends and look at people for a living. The result is a city where
the surveillance is total and entirely mundane, and where privacy is
purchased with distance and mud.

**Where they can be unobserved:**

- **The Shell Bank.** Yannu's hut on a two-mile ridge of dead cockle at the
  Whiting's edge, three hours' walk from any road, in ground no assessor will
  cross. Sensory: white glare that makes you squint indoors; the crust
  ticking as it cools, like a hearth burning in a room with no fire; no
  birds at all; air that dries the eye in a minute; Veth's boots on a nail.
- **The Third Reach at low water.** The two hours the survey works. Nobody
  else has business on that mud. Sensory: black silt that pulls at the boot
  and lets go with a sound like a kiss; methane off the drained fen; the
  tide-bell at Kell Ammar counting the hours they have left; sedge that
  hisses when the wind turns.
- **The salt-house at Kell Ammar, in a storm.** One lamp, eleven people, and
  a room where the only privacy is that everybody is pretending to sleep.
  Sensory: coarse salt gritting underfoot; wet wool; the roof taking it; a
  conversation held at the volume of breathing across four yards of floor.

**Where they cannot:**

- **The Stone Ait** — assessors in every corridor, and Sahra's cuticles are
  a public document.
- **The Sarrow villages** — 1,900 people who know exactly what she is
  composed to and consider it their business, because it is.
- **The Low Wharfs** — Nesuir factors on every wharf, and Dovra pays for
  reports the way other people pay for tea.

---

## Internal Consistency Rules

Hard constraints. A draft that violates one of these has broken the book.

1. **Nothing new in the last quarter.** Every capability used at the Wallow
   in ch 43–44 is on the page by ch 23: the live pass (ch 15), foundering
   (ch 9), the jump (ch 8, ch 30), grey as keeping (ch 2, ch 18), the
   House's obligation to credit a witnessed working on its own account
   (ch 3, ch 20).
2. **No relays.** HR-8 is absolute. No second setter ever takes over. The
   High Tower Surprise in ch 40 exists *because* of this rule, not despite
   it.
3. **No reversals.** Grey does not come back. Capacity does not come back.
   Turi does not recover. Sarrow-under-Wall is not resettled. Nothing paid
   in this book is refunded, on the page or in the epilogue.
4. **Sensations are fixed.** The signatures in §Costs are the only ones. A
   load does not develop a new symptom because a scene wants a mood.
5. **The tide governs.** No set above the tideline, none in moving water,
   none at flood. The largest workings need the lowest tides, and the lowest
   tides of 1219 fall in Deepwinter. Anyone who wants to work bigger has to
   wait for the water, and the book never suspends this for convenience.
6. **Travel times are real.** Kethren is nine days up and four down. A
   letter and its answer is three weeks. Nobody arrives early because the
   plot wants them.
7. **Rank.** The Chief Reckoner outranks any house. A house outranks a
   fen-reeve. A standing order outranks a private contract. The Third Order
   outranks sentiment, including Halim's.
8. **Absence is noticed.** A composed drawer missing from a standing order is
   reported by the under-reckoner at the next tide, not next week. Any scene
   in which the two of them are alone must account for where the House
   thinks they are.
9. **Irreversible by design:** foundering, grey, a jump, a recorded refusal
   at a witnessing, a distrained tenancy, an entry struck in the Long Book.

**Escapes this book must not use.**

- A hidden capacity in Sahra that turns out to be larger than fourteen
  because the climax needs it. She founders at the Wallow. That is the point.
- A second sink discovered in the outer isles. Sur Ellun failed in 1148 and
  stays failed.
- The House repealing the Third Order, reforming itself, or being overthrown.
  It survives the book intact and more powerful.
- Dovra Nesuir relenting, dying conveniently, or being revealed as corrupt.
  She is solvent, honest, and immovable, and she is still standing on the
  last page.
- Any tie between the leads that reports a feeling. HR-11 reports a fact and
  nothing else, ever.
- A working that costs less than the price list says because the chapter is a
  tender one.
